name: LongText-Bench
intro: LongText-Bench 是 X-Omni 提出的中英双语图像长文本渲染基准。它以标牌、物体标签、印刷品、网页、幻灯片、海报、字幕和对话八类场景构建 160 个双语提示概念，官方数据分别提供 160 条英文和 160 条中文记录。每个提示生成 4 张图，Qwen2.5-VL-7B 识别文字后按英文词或中文字符做无序多重集合匹配，并以文字准确率评分。
build_method: GPT-4o按八类生成长短提示, 中英配对, 逐条人工复核与长度平衡
task_type: 图像生成, 长文本渲染, OCR评测
eval_feature: 每提示四图, Qwen2.5-VL-7B OCR, 无序词/字符匹配
task_type_en: Image generation, long-text rendering, OCR evaluation
build_method_en: GPT-4o short/long prompt generation across eight scenarios, paired English and Chinese records, per-prompt human review and length balancing
eval_feature_en: Four images per prompt, Qwen2.5-VL-7B OCR, unordered word/character matching
intro_en: LongText-Bench is the bilingual image long-text rendering benchmark introduced by X-Omni. It defines 160 bilingual prompt concepts across signs, labeled objects, printed materials, web pages, slides, posters, captions, and dialogues; the official data provide 160 English and 160 Chinese records. Four images are generated per prompt, Qwen2.5-VL-7B recognizes their text, and Text Accuracy is computed with unordered multiset matching over English words or Chinese characters.

drawio_review_note: Aligned with X-Omni arXiv:2507.22058 Appendix C.2, the official X-Omni-Team/X-Omni evaluator, and the X-Omni/LongText-Bench dataset card and JSONL release. The benchmark defines eight text-rich scenarios—signboards, objects with labels, printed materials, web pages, slides, posters, captions, and dialogues—and uses GPT-4o to create 20 English prompts per scenario, ten short and ten long. Every prompt is manually reviewed and rendered-text lengths are adjusted for balance: English short 10–30 and long 30–50 words; Chinese short 20–40 and long typically over 60 characters. The release pairs 160 English records with 160 Chinese records sharing prompt IDs, so it represents 160 bilingual prompt concepts / 320 language records. Evaluation samples four images per language-specific prompt, OCRs them with Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct up to 1,024 new tokens, removes punctuation, lowercases and whitespace-normalizes English or retains Chinese/alphanumeric characters, and computes a micro-averaged matched-ground-truth ratio using unordered word multisets for English and character multisets for Chinese. This deliberately avoids edit distance because OCR output does not preserve relative text-segment order.
